environment.build: Release with IPO for both runners and JIT libraries

protocol.pmu: Pinned current-thread group: userspace retired instructions, cycles, branches, branch misses; all enabled/running times equal; no multiplex scaling
protocol.timing: Same callable kernels and full output validation as comparison; 21 fresh process pairs, three warm invocations per process
protocol.sampling: Separate diagnostic runs, 3 fresh processes per engine/kernel, 60 warm invocations each; PERF_COUNT_SW_CPU_CLOCK 250 us IP sampling
protocol.variants: Alternate guest kernels identify sensitivities; output contract is checked, final NZCV is not part of that contract
protocol.isolated_phases: Compute phases separately recompiled; their timings and differences are not an exact additive partition of the original workload
protocol.scalar_controls: Disabling vectorizers occurs after -O2; both code generation and full output are checked
protocol.code_dumps: SwiftVM compile/publication callbacks observe IR and actual published bytes without changing IR; Dynarmic public disassembly API; diagnostic hooks run outside warm timers

integer_hot_loop.note: Static taken-path categories cross-checked against retired PMU instruction counts; not time percentages.

limitations: WSL finite workloads, CPU frequency not locked; ratios do not prove full application performance.
Retired instructions are dynamic PMU values; instructions-per-cycle explains throughput, not per-mechanism time percentages.
Alternate guest loops and separate phase compilation preserve output only; effects must not be added as independently removable costs.
CPU-clock sampling is intrusive and may attribute stall time to the following instruction; sampled timings are excluded from headline measurements.
Symbol-based numeric classification includes the numeric helper closure; shared-library samples remain separate when exact symbols are unavailable.
A native x64 FP path must preserve ARM FPCR/FPSR and boundary behavior; replacing the helper wholesale is not established as correct by these measurements.
